name: Primary Progressive Apraxia of Speech

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Progressive Apraxia of Speech

criteria.description: Insidious onset and gradual progression of apraxia of speech characterized by impaired planning and programming of speech movements
Minimal or no evidence of aphasia in early stages to distinguish from primary progressive aphasia
Presence of distorted sound substitutions, articulatory groping, and slow speech rate with segmentation
Neuroimaging showing focal atrophy or hypometabolism in premotor and supplementary motor areas
Exclusion of alternative causes such as stroke, tumor, or other neurodegenerative diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive speech disturbance with characteristic apraxic features and minimal aphasia, supported by clinical and neuroimaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of other neurodegenerative and acquired causes of speech impairment.

imaging: Focal atrophy in the left premotor and supplementary motor cortex on MRI
Hypometabolism in premotor regions on FDG-PET
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; some overlap with tauopathies
other: Speech-language pathology assessment confirming apraxia of speech features

distinguishingFeatures: Prominent language comprehension or naming deficits
Less prominent motor speech planning impairment
Predominant dysarthria with consistent weakness or spasticity
Imaging evidence of focal vascular lesion

redFlags: Early prominent limb weakness or sensory loss
